Please explain any activities and/or experiences that demonstrate your commitment to the LGBT civil rights movement. My efforts as an Assemblywoman are rooted in amplifying marginalized and underrepresented voices. I am deeply committed to social justice, equality and opportunity for all. I have been an Assemblywoman for three terms and have authored and passed dozens of bills including: --Lowering the age requirement of New York City Community Board membership to 16 years old, effectively allowing 16 and 17 year olds to participate in local planning boards --Expanding the Bus Rapid Transit Program in New York City; banning styrofoam; expanding the Green Roof Tax Abatement with a lens toward environmental justice in underserved communities --Requiring a report into the feasibility of instituting flexible work schedules in state agencies --Ensuring access to rehabilitative programming in state correctional facilities for women inmates are equivalent to programs afforded to men --Expanding the use of standby guardianship to include instances of immigration-related arrest, detention, and deportation --Requiring New York to undertake the first study of homeless veterans --Allowing local law enforcement to remove guns/firearms from homes where a domestic violence incident has occurred My approach to community building has consistently reflected my position as a firm ally of any and all LGBT individuals. As such, I wholeheartedly support progressive legislation that advances rather than reverses the fundamental right of LGBT individuals to be treated as equals under the scope of state law.

Please explain any activities and/or experiences that demonstrate your commitment to the LGBT civil rights movement. I identify an as ally of the LGBTQIA+ community. My pronouns are he/him/his. I'm proud of the following 1) As Vice President of NYCEDC, I personally oversaw the modernization of the LGBT Center for the city. I recall walking into the space with staff working under garbage bags that was catching rain drops from the leaking roof/ceiling. It's an incredible accomplishment for the community which facility that honors it's rich history and a powerful symbol of the civil rights movement. 2) Most recently I worked as a nonprofit lobbyist and represented organizations that helped to expand PrEP access, facilitated a special hearing on Ending the Epidemic to coincide with World Aids Day, increase funding for workforce development programs that employed HIV+ individuals, created more drop in center for LGBT youth who have been kicked out of their homes, and expand health insurance coverage for LGBT individuals. I'm glad to have had this opportunity to directly and meaningfully fight with some of the leading nonprofits in NYC for legislation, funding and policy for the LGBT community.

I was honored to march with them in multiple Pride Parades including Word Pride, and to attend community programs and invite others to learn about their work. We have a tremendous amount of work to do breaking down discrimination and others biases with cultural competence locally. In the Assembly, I would be eager to support their growth across the district and continue to partner with them. 4) I have also created platforms and used many opportunities to spotlight discrimination within Guyana, and to empower local organizations at the forefront of the equal rights movement there. This is important to me because it is where I first saw the destructive and violent potential of homophobia. What experience do you have to demonstrate you are the best person to represent the office you seek? I came to the United States as an undocumented dreamer, joining my family who were working multiple jobs, without any health insurance and growing up in illegal housing. These issues have not gone away even 25 years later, and in many cases they're even greater. It is an accomplishment to become a legal resident with the help of my family. I'm in public service to fight for working class families, like my own, to improve our district. Working in the public sector for over 10 year and rising up into leadership has shown me how government can be tremendously effective, and sometimes, who is left out of the process, often communities like AD 31. As a Vice President of NYCEDC, I oversaw over $1.2B annually in funding for projects and communities across the five boroughs. As a chief of staff at the Administration for Children's Services, I spearheaded a set of reforms to improve the agency's relationship with nonprofit partners and to improve outcomes for children and families. At the Department of Consumer Affairs, I led the launch and implementation of a program to help working families save money on federal taxes though their employer. Within the community, I volunteered for over a decade on the community board, organized protests and rallies by mobilizing my neighbors, and co-created a nonprofit organization that helped hundreds of Indo-Caribbean and other communities of color to succeed. I teach history to young adults at York College because this story is often not told, and not told by us. In the Assembly, I'm looking

Yes Section 2: CANDIDATE EXPERIENCE (Short Answer) Please provide brief responses to each of the following questions - cite specific examples of your policy proposals and/or previous actions as applicable. Please explain any activities and/or experiences that demonstrate your commitment to the LGBT civil rights movement. I have a long track record of commitment to LGBTQIA+ liberation. I personally identify as a part of the LGBTQIA+ community and have fought for decades for health, dignity and justice for LGBTQIA+ people, particularly immigrants, Latinxs and queer people of color. In my community, I have long supported LGBTQIA+ leaders and organizations, and have participated in our local Queens Pride parade since 2001 - marching either as a former elected official (Democratic State Committee Member), or with organizations, such a New Immigrant Community Empowerment (NICE). In the late ‘90s/early 2000s, I showed up alongside the LGBTQIA+ community in Queens when Julio Rivera and Edgar Garzon were separately murdered in Jackson Heights, attending vigils and events that honored their lives, and worked with (then-District Leader) Danny Dromm and the Garzon family to demand that the police investigate Edgar’s murder. I have always supported and championed policies that advance the civil rights of the LGBTQIA+ community and as the former leader of the National Latina Institute for Reproductive Justice, I ensured that all our policy work incorporated an LGBTQIA+ lens. For example, we were one of the first reproductive justice organizations to serve as bold advocates for the reproductive health needs of Latinx trans men,

[PDF page 12] 2020 State Candidate Questionnaire Responses noting that dignified gynecological care, pap smears and birth control were health services that trans men needed access to, and we fought to ensure it was also culturally-competent, linguistically appropriate and accessible, despite immigration status. Another policy priority was fighting for the civil rights provision of the Affordable Care Act (section 1557) which included sexual orientation and gender identity as protected classes. I’ve invested sponsorship funding and served on committees for the Latinx Pre-Conference Institute of Creating Change Conference (the largest LGBTQ annual conference in the country) and regularly presented on panels regarding the intersections of LGBTQIA+ liberation, reproductive justice and immigration, once serving as a plenary speaker. I’ve served on countless coalitions alongside LGBTQIA+ organizations, hosted numerous congressional briefings on LGBTQIA+ health, written op-eds advocating for queer-friendly policies and thought pieces on intersectionality (here is 2012 example from the Huffington Post: https://www.huffpost.com/entry/latino-lgbtq_b_1640055) and have built deep partnerships with leaders across movements. Lastly, I ensure my organization’s policies and practices aligned with values that we promoted and that such policies that used language that was gender-neutral and inclusive, such as ‘parental leave’ instead of ‘maternity leave.’ I am proud to have hired queer- identified and trans staff throughout the organization, serving in both leadership and management positions. This is the approach I plan to take forward into the New York State Assembly. What experience do you have to demonstrate you are the best person to represent the office you seek? As the daughter of an immigrant father from Paraguay and a Puerto Rican mother, I am a fierce advocate for people of color, immigrants, and LGBTQIA+ communities. Corona, East Elmhurst, Jackson Heights, and Woodside - the communities of the 34th Assembly District - are among the most diverse neighborhoods in the world. I understand that the strength of our Queens community is in its diversity, and I hold an unwavering commitment to progressive values. Through my community activism on immigration, I’ve witnessed the challenges that everyday families face when looking to secure stable housing, raise children, seek dignified work, and succeed in this country. And through my advocacy on gender and reproductive justice, I see how laws deeply impact our ability to make autonomous decisions about our bodies, health, family, and future. I am running for State Assembly because I am an activist both locally and nationally with a proven track record of standing up and speaking out against injustices. For the past 13 years, I have served as the leader of the National Latina Institute for Reproductive Health, an organization dedicated to building Latina power to advance gender justice, becoming a nationally recognized

[PDF page 13] 2020 State Candidate Questionnaire Responses advocate for universal health care and reproductive freedom. It takes a leader who understands and connects to the experiences and struggles of our community to be an effective representative. I am running for State Assembly because we deserve a choice in who represents us. For too long, we have been represented by someone who was handpicked by the party bosses in a rigged process that shut voters out. The incumbent has never had to face a challenger and who does not reflect our values or our diversity. The voters in the 34th Assembly District deserve to experience democracy and have their voices heard. I envision a New York where all people have the opportunity to thrive - to be able to live, learn, work and raise their families with dignity, safety and equity under healthy conditions. Please detail any specific policy proposals you may have that will affect the LGBT community. I see all issues through an intersectional lens, so nearly every issue disproportionately impacts the LGBTQIA+ community - particularly how it relates to discrimination and bias, including criminal justice, education, immigration, economic justice, healthcare, etc. Specifically, I strongly support repealing the Walking while Trans bill, which allows the NYPD to profile primarily black and Latinx trans women, who are often doing nothing more than walking down the street, as sex workers. I would go even further by supporting decriminalizing sex work. Sex work is work, and trans women of color in my community have been disproportionately targeted by the police, putting them in greater danger. In addition, I support ensuring that our healthcare system provides gender-affirming healthcare and that state-issued identification allows for individuals to self-identify a gender that may not be aligned with the gender assigned at birth. In addition, central to my education platform is mandating that all public schools offer comprehensive sex-ed, specifically ensuring that it is age-appropriate, medically accurate, culturally competent, and LGBTQ-affirming. I will utilize discretionary funds to support LGBTQIA+ organizations in the community and am committed to ensuring that my staff is diverse and that there is a strong advocate/liaison to the LGBTQIA+ community in my district office. I am a long-time member of P-FLAG. I march in the Queens Pride Parade every year. In fact, I volunteered for the parade by driving the grand marshal of the Queens Pride parade through entirety of the parade one year. I also march in the St. Pat's for All Parade every year. I have also had the honor of working with several LGBT individuals in my office over the course of my time in the Assembly. One person, who was a dear friend of mine and worked with me at the Office of Emergency Management in the aftermath of the 9/11 attacks, unfortunately passed away. Another LGBT staffer recently left my office to work at the New York City Council One of my newest staffers, whom I hired to liaise with the community and work on casework, is a member of the LGBT community. I have also worked closely with Alfonso Quiroz of Out Jackson Heights on numerous LGBT issues in Jackson Heights.

What experience do you have to demonstrate you are the best person to represent the office you seek? In my time representing the 34th Assembly District since 2009, I have amplified the voices of those who are most vulnerable and who are often underserved by government, including immigrants, those of a lower socioeconomic status, and the LGBTQ community. I have authored a bill (A9552) that would prevent life insurance companies from discriminating against HIV-positive individuals by mandating that life insurance companies no longer ask about testing positive for HIV on life insurance questionnaires. I worked closely with Assembly Member Daniel O'Donnell and LGBT Network President David Kilmnick in rolling out the legislation. [PDF page 117] 2020 State Candidate Questionnaire Responses As the State Senate Candidate, I alone distributed a COVID platform. As COVID- 19 mercilessly sweeps through our City and through the District, our communities of color are disproportionately affected with tragic outcomes that far outnumber non-minority neighborhoods. This pandemic has exposed the systemic failure of adequate and accessible healthcare to address longtime health comorbidities among black, brown, LGBTQ and other minority populations. Tragically the death toll in New York City increases daily by the hundreds, and yet, in our densely populated neighborhoods, untold individuals succumb unreported and unknown. This isn't a new trend, I've sounded the alarm about our medically underserved District for years. Now pressed by the media, some electeds say "the disparities are real and unfortunate" ... I say it's a national disgrace! Still, healthcare access has not improved, Staten Island still has no public hospital, and there are just two testing sites in the North Shore (one by appointment only). Coney Island Hospital, fortunately, continues to serve area residents. My parents taught me and my siblings, literally, to set a table for the poor and the castaway; so we would become "Champions" for the least of us. As such, I am a fierce advocate of worker's rights, economic security, and upholding Union guarantees. I am a TRUE Democrat and an unafraid "Voice for the Voiceless". I was born and raised in the West Brighton neighborhood of Staten Island. For several years, the Edwin Markham Gardens (NYCHA) was home. "The Markham Homes" was a multicultural community of 360 working class families with dreams to thrive, and not to simply exist. For over 30 years as a Human Resources Professional, I have battled Economic Injustice, by connecting the unemployed and underemployed, Veterans, LGBTQ individuals, and Homeless or Sheltered persons, to hundreds of full time jobs. I exposed oppressive policies aimed to diminish Worker Protections and Labor Unions. In so doing, I implemented mandated Worker protection programs, and trained Managers on best practices and supervision, worker education and protections. I am very proud of my reputation as an Intermediary and Problem Solver with Management, Unions and Employees. Community Health Education: To address the disparities in both health outcomes and healthcare access across the 23rd District, I hosted, "Ask The Doctors", a community wellness forum. While a multi-purposed event, one takeaway of this expert panel of NINE Black Male Physicians, remains to excite and encourage young men of color to consider careers in medicine.
